text: My second wife had severe convulsions after an MDMA overdose. At the hospital, they figured out what caused that: her potassium was found to be critically low, and IV potassium was the only treatment they gave her. That experience is what leads me to treat serious MDMA toxicity as a broader electrolyte emergency, although magnesium is still the first and most useful supplement to give once the jaw tenses, since potassium gets depleted once magnesium runs low.
reader: a friend at a festival with someone who took MDMA a few hours ago, whose jaw has started to clench and grind, with magnesium chloride flakes in their bag, reading what to do

sentences.payoff: they treat serious MDMA toxicity as more than a magnesium problem, give magnesium first, and know why potassium follows it

checked.point: magnesium deficiency makes the body lose potassium, so potassium follows magnesium
checked.found: his TEACH-WIFE comment of 2026-11-24 19:53 UTC: "i clarified that magnesium depletion can deplete potassium"; Huang and Kuo 2007 (PubMed 17804670): magnesium deficiency "exacerbates potassium wasting by increasing distal potassium secretion"; the fit read of this turn (reads/fit-a1-sec.txt S12): "after magnesium" can read as the magnesium causing the potassium loss
checked.still_needed: yes: they know giving magnesium is not what drains the potassium

question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
